maryland.label: Maryland
maryland.bookValueRule: If vehicle is under 7 years old and the price is more than $500 below NADA retail, MVA may assess on book value; documentation of the lower price can support taxing it on the price
notes: Title fee increased from $100 to $200 effective July 1, 2025.
Registration fees reflect the 3 statutory passenger/multipurpose weight tiers under Maryland SB 362 (effective July 1, 2024 / 2025).
Private-party sales are taxed on the full agreed price or book value; trade-in deductions are not permitted by MD statute.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Maryland MVA.

Vehicles under 7 years old may be assessed on book value, not your purchase price, when the price is more than $500 below NADA retail. Documentation of the lower sale price can support taxing it on your price.
Maryland taxes the full purchase price — trade-ins and rebates do not reduce excise tax.

faqs.question: Do I pay sales tax on a private car sale in Maryland?
faqs.answer: Yes. In Maryland, private vehicle purchases are subject to a 6.5% vehicle excise tax collected by the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) when you apply for the title certificate. There is a statutory minimum excise tax floor of $41.60 (based on a minimum $640 vehicle valuation).

faqs.question: How much is the Maryland title transfer fee?
faqs.answer: The certificate of title fee in Maryland is $200.00 for both new and used vehicles (increased from $100 on July 1, 2025). If your purchase is financed, an additional $40 security interest (lien) filing fee applies.

faqs.question: How does Maryland calculate vehicle excise tax on private sales?
faqs.answer: For vehicles 7 or more years old, the 6.5% excise tax is calculated on the purchase price, with a minimum taxable value of $640. For vehicles under 7 years old, the tax is also calculated on the purchase price unless the price is more than $500 below the NADA retail book value. In that case the MVA may assess the tax on the book value instead. Documentation of the lower sale price can support taxing it on your price.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce vehicle excise tax in Maryland?
faqs.answer: No. Under Maryland law, trade-in deductions are only permitted on purchases from licensed Maryland motor vehicle dealers. In a private-party sale, the excise tax base is the full purchase price; any trade-in value does not reduce your tax obligation.

faqs.question: How much are Maryland vehicle registration and tag fees?
faqs.answer: Maryland offers both 1-year and 2-year registration terms for Class A (passenger) and Class M (multipurpose) vehicles across three statutory weight tiers under SB 362: vehicles 0–3,500 lbs are $120.50 for 1 year ($241.00 for 2 years); vehicles 3,501–3,700 lbs are $125.50 for 1 year ($251.00 for 2 years); and vehicles over 3,700 lbs are $191.50 for 1 year ($383.00 for 2 years). Class D motorcycles are $105.00 for 1 year or $210.00 for 2 years. Zero-emission electric vehicles (ZEVs) have an additional $125/year surcharge, while plug-in hybrids (PHEVs) have a $100/year surcharge.

faqs.question: Do I pay Maryland vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. When you title the car in Maryland you pay the 6.5% excise tax under the same rules as an in-state purchase, including the book value rule for vehicles under 7 years old. The out-of-state title must meet Maryland standards, and the car may need a Maryland safety inspection before it can be titled and registered.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Maryland?
faqs.answer: Many family gifts are exempt from the 6.5% excise tax when no money changes hands, the car is titled in Maryland, and you file the Gift Certification (Form VR-103). Qualifying relationships include a spouse, parents and stepparents, children (including adopted and stepchildren), siblings and half-siblings, grandparents and grandchildren, and in-laws. An aunt or uncle aged 65 or older can also gift a car tax-free to a niece or nephew. Other transfers may owe excise tax.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Maryland?
faqs.answer: The MVA’s private-sale guidance does not set a separate filing deadline, but you cannot drive the car on the seller’s plates and you must title and register it before driving. The safety inspection certificate is valid for 90 days, and a 30-day temporary registration is available so you can drive the car to an inspection station.

virginia.label: Virginia
virginia.bookValueRule: Vehicles under 5 model years old need an Affidavit for Procurement of Title (SUT-1A) if the sale price is not within $1,500 of the NADA trade-in value.

notes: Virginia levies a 4.15% Motor Vehicle Sales and Use Tax (SUT) with a $75.00 minimum.

Virginia taxes the gross sales price. Trade-ins do not reduce the Motor Vehicle Sales and Use Tax.
Vehicles under 5 model years old need Form SUT-1A if the sale price is not within $1,500 of the NADA trade-in value.
A Highway Use Fee may apply in addition to registration. The calculator includes it only for electric vehicles.

faqs.question: What is the Virginia sales tax on a private car purchase?
faqs.answer: Virginia imposes a 4.15% Motor Vehicle Sales and Use Tax (SUT) based on the gross sales price, with a statutory minimum tax of $75.00.

faqs.question: How much is the title certificate fee in Virginia?
faqs.answer: The Virginia DMV charges $15.00 for an original or transferred certificate of title. If the vehicle is financed, an additional $15.00 supplemental lien filing fee applies.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce sales tax in Virginia?
faqs.answer: No. Under Virginia law (VA Code § 58.1-2401), the Motor Vehicle Sales and Use Tax is calculated on the gross sales price. Trade-in deductions are not permitted on private-party or dealer transactions.

faqs.question: How much are vehicle registration fees in Virginia?
faqs.answer: Virginia passenger vehicle registration is weight-based: $30.75/year for vehicles 4,000 lbs or less ($59.50 for 2 years with the $2 discount) and $35.75/year for vehicles over 4,000 lbs ($69.50 for 2 years). Motorcycles are $24.75/year ($47.50 for 2 years).

faqs.question: Do I pay Virginia vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. Virginia collects its 4.15% Sales and Use Tax (minimum $75) when you title the vehicle in Virginia, based on the sale price. Bring the signed-over out-of-state title, a completed Application for Title and Registration (VSA 17A), proof of address, and proof of the purchase price.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Virginia?
faqs.answer: A gift to a spouse, or to a biological or adopted child or parent, is exempt from the Sales and Use Tax with the Purchaser’s Statement of Tax Exemption (Form SUT 3). Stepchildren, stepparents, siblings, and other relatives do not qualify; for them the tax is based on the NADA trade-in value or the $75 minimum, whichever is greater.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Virginia?
faqs.answer: Virginia law (Code of Virginia § 46.2-630) requires the buyer to send the signed title to the DMV with an application for title and registration within 30 days.

pennsylvania.label: Pennsylvania
pennsylvania.localTaxNote: Pennsylvania sales tax is 6% statewide. Allegheny County residents pay 7% and City of Philadelphia residents pay 8%; the range shows 6% to 8%.
notes: Pennsylvania sales tax is 6% of the purchase price or current market value (7% in Allegheny County, 8% in the City of Philadelphia).
The certificate of title fee is $72.00 and a lien is $36.00 per lien (PennDOT Form MV-70S).
Trade-in credits apply only when a dealer takes the trade-in; private sales are taxed on the full price.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with PennDOT.
Pennsylvania sales tax is 6% statewide (7% in Allegheny County, 8% in the City of Philadelphia).
Private vehicle purchases do not get trade-in tax credits. Tax is owed on the full purchase price or current market value.
Participating counties add a $5 annual fee for local use, collected with registration. It is not included here.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Pennsylvania?
faqs.answer: The Pennsylvania state sales tax rate on motor vehicles is 6% of the purchase price. Residents of Allegheny County pay 7% (additional 1% local tax) and residents of Philadelphia pay 8% (additional 2% local tax).

faqs.question: How much is the Pennsylvania vehicle title transfer fee?
faqs.answer: The certificate of title fee is $72.00 (PennDOT Form MV-70S). If the vehicle is financed, recording a lien adds $36.00 per lien.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce sales tax on private sales in Pennsylvania?
faqs.answer: No. Pennsylvania only allows trade-in credits when you trade a vehicle into a licensed dealership. Private-to-private sales are taxed on the full purchase price or market value without trade-in deduction.

faqs.question: How much is vehicle registration in Pennsylvania?
faqs.answer: Passenger vehicle registration is $48.00 for one year or $96.00 for two years. Motorcycles are $25.00 for one year or $50.00 for two. Participating counties also charge a $5 annual fee for local use, collected with registration.

faqs.question: Do I pay Pennsylvania vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. When you title the vehicle in Pennsylvania you pay Pennsylvania sales tax (6%, or 7% in Allegheny County and 8% in Philadelphia) through an authorized PennDOT agent, along with the title and registration fees.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Pennsylvania?
faqs.answer: A true gift, with no money, property, service, or debt forgiveness in exchange, is exempt from sales tax when both parties complete the Affidavit of Gift (Form MV-13ST). A sale between family members is taxable, and the Department of Revenue may review family sales priced well below fair market value.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Pennsylvania?
faqs.answer: The buyer and seller complete the transfer together at an authorized PennDOT agent (a notary, tag service, or dealer), and the agent must submit the application to PennDOT within 20 days of the sale. A used vehicle must also be inspected within 10 days of sale unless it already has a valid inspection sticker.

delaware.label: Delaware
notes: Delaware has no general sales tax; it assesses a 5.25% Motor Vehicle Document Fee upon titling.
Delaware permits trade-in credit deductions on both dealer and private vehicle purchases (via Form MV347).
Title fee is $35 without a lien and $55 with a lien ($35 title + $20 lien fee).
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Delaware DMV.
Delaware charges a 5.25% Motor Vehicle Document Fee (minimum $8.00) based on net purchase price or NADA average trade-in value.
Trade-in credit is permitted in Delaware: you may deduct the value of your trade-in vehicle from the purchase price before the 5.25% document fee is calculated.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle tax rate in Delaware?
faqs.answer: Delaware does not have a general sales tax. Instead, the Delaware DMV assesses a 5.25% Motor Vehicle Document Fee on the vehicle's purchase price or NADA average trade-in value, whichever is higher (minimum $8.00).

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce the vehicle document fee in Delaware?
faqs.answer: Yes! Delaware law allows you to deduct the value of your trade-in vehicle from the purchase price before calculating the 5.25% document fee. For private sales, buyers can claim this credit using Delaware DMV Form MV347 if completed within 60 days.

faqs.question: How much is a title certificate in Delaware?
faqs.answer: The Delaware DMV title certificate fee is $35.00. If the vehicle is financed with an active lien, the fee is $55.00 ($35 title + $20 lien filing fee).

faqs.question: What are registration fees in Delaware?
faqs.answer: Delaware passenger vehicle registration is $40.00 per year ($80.00 for a 2-year registration). Motorcycle registration is $15.00 per year ($30.00 for 2 years).

faqs.question: Do I pay Delaware vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: When bringing an out-of-state private vehicle into Delaware, the state generally assesses its applicable vehicle sales or use tax (5.25%) upon titling and registration. If you previously paid sales tax in another jurisdiction, many states offer reciprocal tax credit with official proof of payment, though private-sale reciprocity rules vary by statute. Contact the Delaware motor vehicle agency to verify documentation requirements.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Delaware?
faqs.answer: Rules for vehicle transfers or gifts between family members vary significantly by state. In many states, bona fide gifts or transfers between immediate family members (such as spouses, parents, or children) may qualify for tax exemption or reduced fees if accompanied by a sworn gift affidavit or certification, whereas transfers between other relatives or involving debt assumption may remain taxable. Contact the Delaware DMV or Department of Revenue to verify eligibility and required documentation before titling.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Delaware?
faqs.answer: Titling and registration deadlines for private vehicle purchases vary by jurisdiction, typically ranging between 10 to 30 days from the date of purchase. Delaying beyond Delaware's statutory filing deadline can incur late titling penalty fees and restricts legal operation on public roadways. Check with the Delaware motor vehicle agency or your local county title office for the exact filing window and penalty schedule.

district-of-columbia.label: District of Columbia
notes: DC excise tax is assessed on vehicle Fair Market Value (NADA Eastern Region) at rates from 1.0% to 11.0% based on weight and EPA city MPG under the 2025 Act.
The 5.0% baseline rate models a standard passenger car (3,499 lbs or less, 21–25 city MPG).
Trade-ins on private-party sales do not reduce the DC Fair Market Value tax base.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with the DC DMV.
DC calculates vehicle excise tax based on Fair Market Value (NADA Eastern Region) and EPA city MPG tiers ranging from 1.0% to 11.0%. Baseline estimate uses standard 5.0% tier.
District of Columbia taxes full Fair Market Value — private party trade-in values do not reduce excise tax.

faqs.question: How is vehicle excise tax calculated in Washington DC?
faqs.answer: Under DC DMV regulations and the 2025 Motor Excise Tax Amendment Act, excise tax is calculated by multiplying the vehicle's Fair Market Value (NADA Eastern Region Guide) by a percentage determined by unladen weight and EPA city MPG (ranging from 1.0% to 11.0%). Standard passenger vehicles generally fall into the 3.1% to 6.0% range (5.0% average baseline).

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce vehicle excise tax in DC?
faqs.answer: No. In the District of Columbia, excise tax is applied to the vehicle's Fair Market Value; private party trade-in values on a bill of sale do not reduce the assessed tax base.

faqs.question: How much is a title certificate in the District of Columbia?
faqs.answer: The DC DMV certificate of title fee is $26.00. If the vehicle is financed, a $20.00 lien recordation fee applies.

faqs.question: How much are vehicle registration fees in DC?
faqs.answer: DC vehicle registration is weight-based: Class I (3,499 lbs or less) is $72.00 per year ($144.00 for 2 years); Class II (3,500 lbs and over) is $115.00 per year ($230.00 for 2 years). Motorcycle registration is $52.00 per year ($104.00 for 2 years).

faqs.question: Do I pay District of Columbia vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: When bringing an out-of-state private vehicle into District of Columbia, the state generally assesses its applicable vehicle sales or use tax (5.00%) upon titling and registration. If you previously paid sales tax in another jurisdiction, many states offer reciprocal tax credit with official proof of payment, though private-sale reciprocity rules vary by statute. Contact the District of Columbia motor vehicle agency to verify documentation requirements.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in District of Columbia?
faqs.answer: Rules for vehicle transfers or gifts between family members vary significantly by state. In many states, bona fide gifts or transfers between immediate family members (such as spouses, parents, or children) may qualify for tax exemption or reduced fees if accompanied by a sworn gift affidavit or certification, whereas transfers between other relatives or involving debt assumption may remain taxable. Contact the District of Columbia DMV or Department of Revenue to verify eligibility and required documentation before titling.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in District of Columbia?
faqs.answer: Titling and registration deadlines for private vehicle purchases vary by jurisdiction, typically ranging between 10 to 30 days from the date of purchase. Delaying beyond District of Columbia's statutory filing deadline can incur late titling penalty fees and restricts legal operation on public roadways. Check with the District of Columbia motor vehicle agency or your local county title office for the exact filing window and penalty schedule.

california.label: California
california.localTaxNote: California’s 7.25% base rate applies statewide. District taxes in many cities and counties raise the total, up to 11.75% (Lancaster and Palmdale from October 1, 2026). Use tax is based on the address where you register the vehicle.
notes: California’s statewide base sales and use tax rate is 7.25%; district taxes add up to 4.50%.
A private-party transfer costs a $15 transfer fee plus use tax. Registration is $76 plus a $34 CHP fee, a 0.65% vehicle license fee, and a transportation improvement fee of $33 to $231 by value.
Trade-in credit does not apply to private-party sales.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the California DMV or CDTFA.
Use tax is based on the purchase price and the rate where you register the vehicle, and is paid to the DMV at transfer.
Private-party trade-in deductions are not permitted in California.

Registration includes the $76 registration fee, the $34 CHP fee, and estimates of the value-based fees: the vehicle license fee (0.65% of the price, since the DMV bases it on the new owner’s price when a registered vehicle is transferred) and the transportation improvement fee ($33 to $231 by value). Not included: county and district fees and the smog transfer fee.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate on a private car purchase in California?
faqs.answer: California’s statewide base sales and use tax rate is 7.25%. District taxes raise it in many places, up to 11.75% in Lancaster and Palmdale (from October 1, 2026). The rate is based on the address where you register the vehicle.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in California?
faqs.answer: The DMV transfer fee is $15. You also pay use tax on the purchase price when you transfer the title.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce vehicle sales tax in California private sales?
faqs.answer: No. Under California Revenue and Taxation Code Section 6011, trade-in allowances are only recognized when purchasing from licensed retail vehicle dealers. Private-party vehicle sales are taxed on the full purchase price.

faqs.question: How are California vehicle registration fees calculated?
faqs.answer: Registration is $76 (including a $3 alternative fuel and technology fee) plus a $34 CHP fee. Value-based fees are added: a vehicle license fee of 0.65% of the vehicle’s value and a transportation improvement fee from $33 to $231. Zero-emission vehicles from model year 2020 on also pay a $121 road improvement fee.

faqs.question: Do I pay California vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you bring it into California for use here. A vehicle brought in within 12 months of purchase is presumed bought for use in California, and use tax is due when you register it. You may get credit for sales tax paid to another state.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in California?
faqs.answer: A purchase from a parent, grandparent, child, grandchild, spouse, or registered domestic partner is exempt from use tax, and so is a purchase from a brother or sister when both are minors. A true gift with nothing given in return is also exempt. Stepparents and stepchildren qualify only through legal adoption.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in California?
faqs.answer: The buyer has 10 days after the purchase to transfer ownership with the DMV. The seller has 5 days to file a Notice of Transfer and Release of Liability.

texas.label: Texas
texas.bookValueRule: Texas taxes private-party sales on the greater of the sales price or 80% of the Standard Presumptive Value (SPV); a certified appraisal (Form 14-128) obtained within 30 days can lower it.
texas.localTaxNote: Texas charges a flat 6.25% motor vehicle sales tax statewide; local city and county sales taxes do not apply to motor vehicles.
notes: Texas charges a 6.25% motor vehicle sales tax statewide.
Private-party sales are taxed on the greater of the purchase price or 80% of the Standard Presumptive Value (SPV).
Trade-in credit does not apply to private-party sales; it applies only to purchases from a licensed dealer.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Texas Comptroller, TxDMV, or your county tax assessor-collector.
Texas charges 6.25% motor vehicle tax on the greater of the purchase price or 80% of the Standard Presumptive Value (SPV).
Trade-in deductions do not apply to private-party sales in Texas.

Registration shown is the $50.75 base fee (or $54 for 6,001 to 10,000 lbs) plus $1 TexasSure. Also due at registration: a $7.50 inspection program replacement fee, a $4.75 processing fee, a $2.75 emissions fee in 17 counties, and county fees of $0 to $31.50. The title fee is $33 in nonattainment counties and $28 elsewhere.
Texas no longer requires safety inspections for non-commercial vehicles (since January 1, 2025). Vehicles in 17 counties still need an emissions inspection.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Texas for private sales?
faqs.answer: Texas imposes a 6.25% Motor Vehicle Sales and Use Tax. Unlike general retail purchases, motor vehicle sales in Texas are not subject to local city or transit sales taxes.

faqs.question: What is the Standard Presumptive Value (SPV) rule in Texas?
faqs.answer: Private-party sales are taxed on whichever is greater: the price you paid or 80% of the vehicle’s Standard Presumptive Value (SPV). If you paid less, a certified appraisal on Form 14-128, obtained within 30 days of purchase, can lower the taxable value (but not below the price).

faqs.question: Can I deduct a trade-in on a private car sale in Texas?
faqs.answer: No. According to the Texas Comptroller, the trade-in allowance for motor vehicle sales tax only applies when purchasing from a licensed motor vehicle dealer. In a private-party transaction, sales tax must be paid on the full purchase price or Standard Presumptive Value (SPV).

faqs.question: How much are Texas title and registration fees?
faqs.answer: The title application fee is $33 in nonattainment counties and $28 in all other counties. Registration for a car or light truck of 6,000 lbs or less is $50.75 plus $1 TexasSure ($54 plus $1 for 6,001 to 10,000 lbs), plus a $7.50 inspection program replacement fee, a processing fee, and county fees of up to $31.50. Electric vehicles add $200 a year.

faqs.question: Do I pay Texas vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. You pay Texas’s 6.25% motor vehicle tax when you title the vehicle in Texas, on the greater of the price or 80% of its Standard Presumptive Value. Title it in your name within 30 days of the sale.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Texas?
faqs.answer: A gift from a spouse (separate property), parent or stepparent, child or stepchild, sibling, grandparent or grandchild (including in-laws), or guardian is taxed only the $10 gift tax, with a joint notarized Affidavit of Motor Vehicle Gift Transfer (Form 14-317). Gifts from aunts, uncles, nieces, nephews, or cousins, and family sales for money, owe the regular 6.25% motor vehicle tax.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Texas?
faqs.answer: 30 days from the date of sale. After that, a $25 delinquent transfer penalty applies, plus another $25 for each additional month late. Active-duty military get 60 days.

florida.label: Florida
florida.localTaxNote: Most Florida counties add a discretionary sales surtax of 0.5% to 2% (Citrus and Collier have none), based on the buyer’s county of residence. It applies only to the first $5,000 of the price, so it adds at most $100.
notes: Florida state sales tax is 6%.
Title transfer is $75.25 for an electronic title ($77.75 for paper); $85.25 for a used vehicle titled in Florida for the first time.
A $225 initial registration fee (and $28 for a new metal plate) applies when the buyer has no Florida plate to transfer.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Florida Department of Revenue or FLHSMV.
Florida sales tax is 6%. Most counties add a discretionary surtax of 0.5% to 2% on the first $5,000, based on the buyer’s county of residence. The estimate shows the range from no surtax to 2%.
A $225 initial registration fee and $28 metal plate fee apply when the buyer has no Florida plate to transfer. They are included unless you answer Yes to the plate question.
Registration shown is for cars of 2,500 to 3,499 lbs ($35.60) and 3,500 lbs and up ($45.60). Cars under 2,500 lbs pay $27.60.
A trade-in between individuals reduces the taxable price only when vehicles are traded in a single transaction, documented on the bill of sale and titles.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Florida for private party sales?
faqs.answer: Florida charges 6% state sales tax. Most counties add a discretionary sales surtax of 0.5% to 2%, based on the buyer’s county of residence, on only the first $5,000 of the price.

faqs.question: How much is the Florida title transfer fee?
faqs.answer: A title transfer is $75.25 for an electronic title (add $2.50 for a paper title). A used vehicle titled in Florida for the first time costs $85.25. Recording a lien may add $2.

faqs.question: What is the Florida $225 initial registration fee?
faqs.answer: Florida charges a one-time $225 initial registration fee when the owner does not have a Florida license plate, registered in their name from a previously owned vehicle, to transfer. A new metal plate adds $28.

faqs.question: Does Florida allow trade-in credit on private sales?
faqs.answer: Only when two individuals trade vehicles in a single transaction. Then sales tax applies to the difference in value. Selling one car and using the money to buy another is not a trade-in.

faqs.question: Do I pay Florida vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. When you title and register the vehicle in Florida you pay Florida’s 6% sales tax, plus any county surtax. If you paid sales tax in another state, you pay the difference when Florida’s rate is higher.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Florida?
faqs.answer: A gift between individuals is not taxed when no payment is made and no loan is taken over; declare it on the title application with a sworn statement. A sale between relatives is taxed like any other sale.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Florida?
faqs.answer: 30 calendar days, starting the day after the seller completes the title transfer and delivers the vehicle. After that, a late transfer fee applies.

new-york.label: New York
new-york.localTaxNote: New York’s 4% state sales tax plus local tax gives combined rates from 7% to 8.875% (8.875% in New York City). The rate is set by where the buyer lives, and the DMV collects it when you register.
notes: New York’s state sales tax is 4%; local tax brings the combined rate to between 7% and 8.875%.
The title certificate fee is $50. Recording a lien costs $5.
Passenger registration is a 2-year fee set by the vehicle’s weight on the DMV fee chart.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the NYS DMV or the NYS Department of Taxation and Finance.
Sales tax is 4% state tax plus local tax (combined 7% to 8.875%) at the rate where the buyer lives, paid to the DMV with Form DTF-802.

Registration shown is the 2-year fee from the DMV weight chart. Also due on an original registration: $25 for plates. New York City and many counties add a vehicle use tax of $10 to $60 for 2 years, and the 12 counties of the Metropolitan Commuter Transportation District add a $50 supplemental fee for 2 years.
Motorcycle registration is $17.50 a year.
Have the vehicle inspected within 10 days of registering. An inspection issued to the previous owner is not valid.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in New York State?
faqs.answer: New York’s state sales tax is 4%. Local tax brings the combined rate to between 7% and 8.875% (8.875% in New York City). You pay the rate where you live, to the DMV when you register, using Form DTF-802.

faqs.question: How much is a title certificate in New York?
faqs.answer: The title certificate fee is $50. If the vehicle is financed, recording the lien costs $5.

faqs.question: Does New York allow trade-in credit for private car sales?
faqs.answer: A private sale has no trade-in, so sales tax is figured on the full purchase price you report on Form DTF-802.

faqs.question: How often do you renew vehicle registration in New York?
faqs.answer: Passenger registrations run for 2 years. The fee depends on the vehicle’s weight: for example, $56.50 for 3,451 to 3,550 lbs, $69 for 3,951 to 4,050 lbs, and $140 for 6,951 lbs or more. There is a $32.50 minimum for vehicles with 6 or more cylinders and electric vehicles. A new registration also costs $25 for plates, plus county use tax and, in the downstate commuter district, a $50 supplemental fee.

faqs.question: Do I pay New York vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: If you live in New York, you pay New York sales tax when you register the vehicle here. Form DTF-804 gives credit for sales tax already paid to another state only if that state allows the same credit for New York tax. If you were not a New York resident when you bought the vehicle, Form DTF-803 claims the non-resident exemption.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in New York?
faqs.answer: No sales tax is due on a gift, or on a purchase from your spouse, parent, child, stepparent, or stepchild. Claim the exemption on Form DTF-802. For a gift from anyone else, the person giving the vehicle completes section 6 of the form.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in New York?
faqs.answer: Register and title the vehicle at a DMV office before you drive it. Bring the signed title, a bill of sale, Form DTF-802, Form MV-82, and New York insurance, and register within 180 days of the effective date on your insurance card. Get an inspection within 10 days of registering. New residents must register within 30 days of moving to New York.

illinois.label: Illinois
illinois.localTaxNote: Illinois taxes private-party purchases with the flat amounts on Form RUT-50: Table A by vehicle age under $15,000, Table B by price at $15,000 and up. Chicago and Cook County residents also owe local vehicle use taxes based on the vehicle’s age: Chicago $50 to $80 (none at 15 years or older), Cook County $90 to $225. For motorcycles, Chicago charges $15 and Cook County $90.
notes: Private-party vehicle purchases in Illinois are taxed on Form RUT-50, the Private Party Vehicle Use Tax.
Under $15,000 the tax is a flat amount by vehicle age (Table A); at $15,000 and up it is a flat amount by price (Table B). Motorcycles pay a flat $25.
The title fee is $165, and standard passenger plates are $151 a year.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Illinois Department of Revenue or the Illinois Secretary of State.
Illinois taxes private-party purchases on Form RUT-50 with flat amounts: Table A by vehicle age under $15,000, Table B by price at $15,000 and up, and $25 for motorcycles.
Purchases from a spouse or civil union partner, parent, brother, sister, or child are taxed $15 instead.
Passenger registration is $151 a year; electric vehicles pay $100 more.

faqs.question: How is tax calculated on a private vehicle sale in Illinois?
faqs.answer: Illinois taxes private-party purchases on Form RUT-50 with flat amounts, not a percentage. Under $15,000, the tax depends on the vehicle’s age (Table A, from $465 for a vehicle up to 1 year old down to $100 for one over 10 years old). At $15,000 and up, it depends on the price (Table B, from $850 for $15,000 to $19,999.99 up to $10,100 at $1,000,000 or more). Motorcycles pay a flat $25.

faqs.question: How much does a vehicle title cost in Illinois?
faqs.answer: The Illinois Secretary of State charges $165 for an original title. Its fee list shows no separate lien fee.

faqs.question: Can I deduct a trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Illinois?
faqs.answer: No. Form RUT-50 has no trade-in credit. The tax comes from the purchase price and the vehicle’s age.

faqs.question: How much are license plate renewal fees in Illinois?
faqs.answer: Standard passenger plates are $151 a year, and motorcycle plates are $41. Electric vehicles pay $100 more each year.

faqs.question: Do I pay Illinois vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you buy from a private seller and bring the vehicle into Illinois, you file Form RUT-50 and pay the Illinois tax within 30 days of bringing it in, using the same tables.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Illinois?
faqs.answer: A purchase from your spouse or civil union partner, parent, brother, sister, or child (including adopted children) is taxed $15 on Form RUT-50. A gift or transfer with no price is taxed on the vehicle’s fair market value using the regular tables.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Illinois?
faqs.answer: File Form RUT-50 and pay the tax within 30 days of buying the vehicle, then apply for the title and registration with the Secretary of State. New residents have 30 days to title and register their vehicles in Illinois.

ohio.label: Ohio
ohio.localTaxNote: Ohio’s 5.75% state rate plus county tax gives combined rates from 6.50% to 8.25% (October to December 2026). The rate is set by the county where the buyer lives, and the tax is paid to the county clerk of courts when the title is transferred.
notes: Ohio’s state sales tax rate is 5.75%; county tax brings the combined rate to between 6.50% and 8.25%.
The title fee is $18 ($23 in counties that add $5), and it covers noting a lien.
Private sales are taxed on the full price paid, even between family members.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Ohio Department of Taxation, the Ohio BMV, or your county clerk of courts title office.
Ohio charges 5.75% state sales tax plus county tax (combined 6.50% to 8.25%) at the rate of the county where you live, paid to the clerk of courts at title transfer.

Registration shown is the $36 passenger fee ($30 for motorcycles). Also due: an $8 deputy registrar fee and any local permissive tax of up to $30. Electric vehicles add $200 a year, plug-in hybrids $150, and hybrids $100.
Some counties require an E-Check emissions certificate before you can register.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Ohio for private sales?
faqs.answer: Ohio’s state rate is 5.75%. County tax brings the combined rate to between 6.50% and 8.25% (October to December 2026). You pay the rate for the county where you live, to the clerk of courts when the title is transferred.

faqs.question: How much does an Ohio vehicle title transfer cost?
faqs.answer: The certificate of title fee is $18, or $23 in counties that add $5. Noting a lien is included in the title fee. Titles are issued by county clerk of courts title offices, not the BMV.

faqs.question: Does Ohio allow trade-in credit on private car sales?
faqs.answer: No. A private sale is taxed on the full price paid. Ohio’s trade-in credit applies to new vehicles bought from a dealer.

faqs.question: How much is passenger vehicle registration in Ohio?
faqs.answer: Passenger registration is $36 a year and motorcycles are $30, plus an $8 deputy registrar fee and any local permissive tax of up to $30. Electric vehicles add $200 a year, plug-in hybrids $150, and hybrids $100.

faqs.question: Do I pay Ohio vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Ohio gives credit for sales or use tax legally paid to another state, with proof of payment, so you owe only any difference. If you bought the vehicle at least six months before moving to Ohio, no Ohio tax is due when you title it here.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Ohio?
faqs.answer: A sale between family members is taxed if any money or other payment changes hands, on the full amount paid. No tax is due on some transfers with no payment, such as an inheritance through probate court, a transfer-on-death beneficiary, or a divorce decree. For a gift, ask your county clerk of courts title office how to claim it.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Ohio?
faqs.answer: Transfer the title at a county clerk of courts title office within 30 days of the sale; a late application costs $5 more. The seller’s signature on the title must be notarized. New residents have 30 days after establishing residency to transfer their title and registration to Ohio.

georgia.label: Georgia
georgia.localTaxNote: Georgia charges a one-time Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT) of 7.0% in place of sales tax and annual property tax. The rate is the same in every county.
notes: TAVT is 7.0% of the vehicle’s fair market value. On a private sale, the Department of Revenue uses the value in the state assessment manual, not the price you paid.
The title fee is $18, and a lien is recorded with it at no extra charge. The license plate is $20 a year, for cars and motorcycles alike.
All-electric vehicles pay a $238.59 alternative fuel fee each year (July 2026 to June 2027). Plug-in hybrids pay it only if they choose the alternative fuel plate.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Georgia Department of Revenue or your County Tag Office.

Georgia taxes a private sale on the fair market value from the state assessment manual, which can be more or less than the price you paid. The estimate uses the price you enter. To match the Department of Revenue, look up the value with its TAVT estimator and enter that value as the price.
A trade-in lowers TAVT only on a dealer sale. Private sales get no trade-in reduction.
New Georgia residents pay 3% instead of 7%. A transfer between immediate family members can pay 0.5% if the previous owner paid TAVT (Form MV-16).
Registration shown is the $20 annual plate fee. All-electric vehicles add the $238.59 alternative fuel fee.

faqs.question: What is the Georgia Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT)?
faqs.answer: A one-time 7.0% tax paid when you title a vehicle, in place of sales tax and annual property tax. It is due with the title application at the County Tag Office in the county where you live.

faqs.question: Is TAVT based on the price I paid in a private sale?
faqs.answer: No. For a used vehicle, the Department of Revenue uses the fair market value in the state assessment manual, which averages wholesale and retail values. You can look it up with the DOR’s TAVT estimator.

faqs.question: Can I deduct a trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Georgia?
faqs.answer: No. The Department of Revenue reduces TAVT for a trade-in only when the sale is made by a dealer.

faqs.question: How much are Georgia title and tag fees?
faqs.answer: The title is $18, and adding a lien is included in that fee. The license plate is $20 a year for a passenger car or a motorcycle.

faqs.question: I am moving to Georgia. What do I pay?
faqs.answer: New residents pay TAVT at 3% of fair market value, plus the $18 title and $20 plate. Register within 30 days of moving, after getting a Georgia driver’s license or ID.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxed in Georgia?
faqs.answer: A transfer between immediate family members (spouse, parent, child, stepchild, sibling, grandparent, grandchild) can pay 0.5% of fair market value if the previous owner paid TAVT. Both sides sign Form MV-16 before a notary.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title a private vehicle purchase in Georgia?
faqs.answer: The Department of Revenue’s private sale page says to title and register within 7 days of purchase. Its fee schedule adds a $10 penalty if you do not apply for the title within 30 days, and TAVT paid late on a private sale carries a 10% penalty after day 30.

north-carolina.label: North Carolina
north-carolina.localTaxNote: North Carolina charges a 3% highway use tax in place of sales tax, with no local rate. Some counties add a small registration tax (up to $17 in Wake, Durham, and Orange).
notes: The highway use tax is 3%. On a private sale it is figured on the vehicle’s market value from the NCDMV schedule, less any trade-in the seller allows.
The title fee is $66.75. Private passenger registration is $46.25 a year ($29.50 for motorcycles).
Electric vehicles add $214.50 a year and plug-in hybrids add $107.25.
Wake, Durham, and Orange counties add $17 a year in county and regional registration taxes; Randolph adds $2.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with NCDMV.
On a private sale, North Carolina figures the 3% highway use tax on market value from the NCDMV value schedule, which may not match the price you paid. The estimate uses the price you enter.

There is no cap for passenger vehicles. The $250 maximum applies only to a vehicle already titled in your name in another state for at least 90 days, and the $2,000 maximum only to commercial vehicles over 26,000 pounds.

Registration shown is the $46.25 passenger fee ($29.50 for motorcycles) plus any EV ($214.50) or plug-in hybrid ($107.25) fee. County and regional registration taxes, and the county property tax collected with registration, are not included.
A lien listed on your title application is recorded with the title. NCDMV charges $25 to add a lien to an existing title later.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle tax rate in North Carolina?
faqs.answer: North Carolina charges a 3% highway use tax instead of sales tax each time a title is transferred. There is no local rate.

faqs.question: Is the highway use tax based on the price I paid in a private sale?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. For a sale by someone who is not a dealer, the tax is figured on the vehicle’s market value, which NCDMV sets from its value schedule, less any trade-in allowance the seller gives you.

faqs.question: Is the North Carolina highway use tax capped?
faqs.answer: Not for a passenger vehicle bought in a sale. A $250 maximum applies when you bring a vehicle that has been titled in your name in another state for at least 90 days. The $2,000 maximum is only for commercial vehicles over 26,000 pounds.

faqs.question: How much are North Carolina title and registration fees?
faqs.answer: The title is $66.75. Registration for a private passenger vehicle is $46.25 a year and $29.50 for a motorcycle. Electric vehicles add $214.50 and plug-in hybrids $107.25. Some counties add up to $17 in registration taxes.

faqs.question: I am moving to North Carolina. What do I pay?
faqs.answer: If the vehicle has been titled in your name in another state for at least 90 days, the highway use tax is capped at $250. You have 60 days after moving to get a North Carolina license and then title and register the vehicle.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in North Carolina?
faqs.answer: A gift between spouses, a parent and child, or a stepparent and stepchild is exempt from the highway use tax with Form MVR-613. The exemption applies to a North Carolina title transferred between North Carolina residents.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title a private vehicle purchase in North Carolina?
faqs.answer: Apply within 28 days of the sale or delivery date, whichever is later, to avoid a $20 late penalty.

michigan.label: Michigan
michigan.localTaxNote: Michigan’s 6% tax applies statewide, on the full purchase price or the vehicle’s fair market value, whichever is greater. The Secretary of State collects it when you transfer the title.
notes: Michigan charges 6% on the full purchase price or fair market value, whichever is greater.
The title transfer fee is $15. Transfer the title within 15 days of the sale or pay a $15 late fee.
Registration for 1984 and newer cars is set by the original list price (MSRP) and drops 10% a year for three years.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Michigan Secretary of State or the Michigan Department of Treasury.
Michigan charges 6% on the full purchase price or fair market value, whichever is greater. The estimate uses the price you enter.

Registration shown is the statutory registration tax for the list price entered (MCL 257.801), assuming the vehicle was first registered in its model year. Plate, plate transfer ($10 to $15), and processing fees are added at the office.
Electric vehicles pay $267 a year more and plug-in hybrids $113.
The seller keeps the plate. You transfer a plate you own or buy a new one.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax rate on a private vehicle purchase in Michigan?
faqs.answer: Michigan charges 6% on the full purchase price or the vehicle’s fair market value, whichever is greater. You pay it to the Secretary of State when you transfer the title.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Michigan?
faqs.answer: The title transfer fee is $15. If you transfer the title more than 15 days after the sale, a $15 late fee is added.

faqs.question: Does Michigan allow trade-in deductions on private car sales?
faqs.answer: A private sale is taxed on the full purchase price or fair market value, whichever is greater.

faqs.question: How are vehicle registration fees calculated in Michigan?
faqs.answer: For 1984 and newer cars, the registration tax is set by the original list price (MSRP): $36 up to $6,000, rising to $178 at $30,000, plus $6 for each $1,000 above that. It drops 10% a year for the next three years, then stays level. Electric vehicles add $267 a year and plug-in hybrids $113.

faqs.question: Do I pay Michigan vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. When you title the vehicle in Michigan, you pay the 6% tax on the full purchase price or fair market value, whichever is greater.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Michigan?
faqs.answer: No tax is due when the new owner is the previous owner’s spouse, parent, child, brother or sister (including half-siblings), grandparent, grandchild, stepparent, stepchild, stepbrother or stepsister, father-, mother-, brother-, sister-, son-, or daughter-in-law, legal ward, or legal guardian. Cousins, aunts, uncles, nieces, and nephews do not qualify. The Department of Treasury may ask for proof of the relationship.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Michigan?
faqs.answer: Transfer the title within 15 days of the sale. After that, a $15 late fee applies. New residents must title and register their vehicles as soon as they establish residency; there is no grace period.

new-jersey.label: New Jersey
new-jersey.localTaxNote: New Jersey’s 6.625% sales tax is the same statewide; there is no local vehicle sales tax.
notes: Private sales are taxed at 6.625% of the purchase price, paid at the Motor Vehicle Commission when you transfer the title.
The title fee is $60, or $85 with one lien.
Passenger registration is $46.50 under 3,500 lbs and $71.50 over 3,500 lbs, or $59 and $84 if the model year is within 2 years. Motorcycles are $65.

Zero emission vehicles pay an extra annual fee set by a statutory schedule: $250 from July 1, 2024, rising $10 each July to $290. That schedule puts it at $270 for July 2026 to June 2027; the MVC has not published that figure itself.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission or the Division of Taxation.
Sales tax is 6.625% of the price you paid. The Division of Taxation’s Casual Sales Unit may question a price well below market value and use NADA values if you do not respond.
There is no trade-in credit on a private sale. Swapping vehicles is taxed on fair market value.

Registration shown uses MVC’s weight classes and the higher fee for model years within 2 years. The $270 zero emission vehicle fee is worked out from the statutory schedule ($250 in July 2024 plus $10 a year), not a figure the MVC publishes.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax on a private car sale in New Jersey?
faqs.answer: 6.625% of the purchase price, paid at a Motor Vehicle Commission agency when you transfer the title.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in New Jersey?
faqs.answer: The title is $60, or $85 for a financed vehicle with one lien ($110 with two liens).

faqs.question: Does New Jersey allow a trade-in credit on a private sale?
faqs.answer: No. Anything of value traded for a car is taxable, and a swap between private parties is taxed on fair market value.

faqs.question: How much is New Jersey registration?
faqs.answer: For a passenger car, $46.50 under 3,500 lbs and $71.50 over, or $59 and $84 if the model year is within 2 years. Motorcycles are $65. Zero emission vehicles also pay an annual fee: the statute sets $250 from July 2024 rising $10 a year, which works out to $270 for July 2026 to June 2027.

faqs.question: I am moving to New Jersey. Do I pay sales tax on my car?
faqs.answer: Not if you bought, titled, and registered it in another state while you lived there. Transfer the title and registration within 60 days of moving.

faqs.question: Is a gifted car taxed in New Jersey?
faqs.answer: No, if it is a genuine gift: the purchase price line on the title must say “GIFT.” If the car still has a loan, tax is due on the loan amount you take over, unless you were already a co-owner.

faqs.question: How long do I have to transfer a title after buying from a private seller?
faqs.answer: Within 10 working days of the sale, in person at a motor vehicle agency, to avoid a $25 penalty.

washington.label: Washington
washington.localTaxNote: Washington adds the local sales tax rate where you live: 1.1% to 4.2% from October 1 to December 31, 2026. In the Sound Transit district, the regional transit authority excise tax is also added to registration each year; it is not included here.
notes: The state rate on a vehicle is 7.0%: the 6.5% sales and use tax plus the 0.5% motor vehicle sales and use tax (0.3% through 2025). The local rate where you live is added.

Use tax is figured on fair market value. Your price is accepted if it is no more than 20% below fair market value or the value is under $7,500. Otherwise you can document a lower value with a pricing guide, a repair estimate, or an appraisal.
From July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, an 8% luxury motor vehicle tax also applies to the part of the price above $102,000.
The title costs $39.50: the $15 application fee, the $6.50 filing fee, and the $18 service fee.

Annual tabs are $82.75 for a vehicle up to 4,000 lbs: the $30 license fee, the $35 weight fee, $6 filing, $11 service, and the $0.75 license service fee. The weight fee is $65 from 4,001 to 6,000 lbs, which makes $112.75.
A buyer gets new plates: $50 per plate plus $2 per plate for reflectivity, so $104 for a car and $22 for a motorcycle. Moving a plate you already own costs $10.
Vehicles that plug in and go at least 30 miles on battery pay $225 a year at renewal ($100, $50, and the $75 transportation electrification fee). Other hybrids pay $75.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Washington Department of Licensing (DOL) or Department of Revenue (DOR).
The estimate uses the price you enter. Washington may tax fair market value instead when the price is more than 20% below it and the value is $7,500 or more.
Local rates change each quarter. The range shown is for October 1 to December 31, 2026.

Registration shown is the state fees for a vehicle up to 6,000 lbs. The regional transit authority excise tax, transportation benefit district fees, and other local fees are not included. DOL’s tab fee estimator gives the exact amount.
DOL’s use tax page still lists the motor vehicle tax at 0.3%. DOR lists 0.5% from January 1, 2026, and the estimate uses 0.5%.

faqs.question: What is the tax on a private car purchase in Washington?
faqs.answer: You pay use tax when you transfer the title: the 7.0% state rate (6.5% plus the 0.5% motor vehicle tax) and the local rate where you live, 1.1% to 4.2% in late 2026. Above $102,000, an 8% luxury tax also applies to the amount over that figure.

faqs.question: Is Washington use tax based on the price I paid?
faqs.answer: Usually. Washington taxes fair market value, but it accepts your price if it is no more than 20% below fair market value or the value is under $7,500. If you paid less because of the vehicle’s condition, a pricing guide value, a repair estimate, or an appraisal can support the lower price.

faqs.question: How much are Washington title and registration fees?
faqs.answer: The title is $39.50 ($15 application, $6.50 filing, and $18 service). Tabs are $82.75 a year for a vehicle up to 4,000 lbs and $112.75 from 4,001 to 6,000 lbs. Plug-in vehicles that go 30 miles or more on battery add $225 at renewal. Local fees, including the regional transit authority tax in the Sound Transit district, are extra.

faqs.question: Do I keep the seller’s license plates in Washington?
faqs.answer: No. A buyer gets new plates at $50 each plus $2 per plate for reflectivity ($104 for a car, $22 for a motorcycle), or moves a plate they already own for $10. The plates can stay on the vehicle when it comes from a spouse or domestic partner, or as a gift or inheritance from a family member.

faqs.question: I am moving to Washington. Do I pay use tax on my car?
faqs.answer: Not if you acquired and used the vehicle as a resident of another state more than 90 days before you came to Washington. You have 30 days after moving to get a Washington driver license and register the vehicle, and the license comes first.

faqs.question: Is a gifted vehicle taxable in Washington?
faqs.answer: A gift or inheritance is exempt when the previous owner paid Washington sales or use tax and nothing is given in return. A vehicle with a loan on it generally does not qualify. A gift from a place without sales tax, such as Oregon, pays use tax unless the giver owned it for at least 7 years in a state or province with sales tax.

faqs.question: How long do I have to transfer the title in Washington?
faqs.answer: You have 15 days. The penalty is $50 on the 16th day and $2 a day after that, up to $125.

arizona.label: Arizona
arizona.localTaxNote: Arizona does not charge sales or use tax on a casual sale between individuals. The yearly cost is the vehicle license tax (VLT), which is figured from the original list price and the vehicle’s age.
notes: A casual sale between individuals is not subject to Arizona sales (transaction privilege) tax or use tax. A vehicle bought from an out-of-state dealer can owe use tax at registration.
The title fee is $4. Registration is $8 ($9 for a motorcycle) plus the $1.50 air quality fee.

The vehicle license tax is paid every year in place of property tax. In the first year it is $2.80 per $100 of 60% of the manufacturer’s base retail price. Each later year the value drops 16.25% and the rate is $2.89 per $100, with a $10 minimum.
The plate stays with the seller, who moves it to another vehicle or turns it in within 30 days.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with Arizona MVD or an authorized third party provider.
The vehicle license tax is estimated from the list price you enter and the model year. MVD counts the years from the vehicle’s first registration, so your bill can differ.
Motorcycles also pay the vehicle license tax, which this estimate does not include for them.
Emissions testing fees in the Phoenix and Tucson areas are not included.

faqs.question: Do I pay sales tax on a private car purchase in Arizona?
faqs.answer: No. A casual sale between individuals is not subject to Arizona sales (transaction privilege) tax or use tax. You still pay the title and registration fees and the vehicle license tax.

faqs.question: What fees do I pay at MVD after a private purchase in Arizona?
faqs.answer: A $4 title fee, $8 for registration ($9 for a motorcycle), the $1.50 air quality fee, and the vehicle license tax.

faqs.question: What is the Arizona vehicle license tax (VLT)?
faqs.answer: It is a yearly tax paid with registration in place of property tax. The first year it is $2.80 per $100 of 60% of the manufacturer’s base retail price. Each later year the value is 16.25% lower and the rate is $2.89 per $100. The minimum is $10.

faqs.question: Do I owe Arizona tax on a car I buy out of state?
faqs.answer: Not from a private seller. From an out-of-state dealer, MVD checks whether tax was paid in the state of purchase. If none was paid, or it was less than Arizona’s use tax, use tax is collected when you register.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Arizona?
faqs.answer: There is no sales tax on a transfer between individuals, family or not. The new owner pays the title fee, registration, and the vehicle license tax.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title a private vehicle purchase in Arizona?
faqs.answer: Apply for the title and registration within 15 days after the seller signs the title over to you.

faqs.question: Do I keep the seller’s license plate in Arizona?
faqs.answer: No. In Arizona the plate stays with the seller, who must move it to another vehicle or turn it in within 30 days. You get a plate when you register.

tennessee.label: Tennessee
tennessee.localTaxNote: Tennessee adds the local rate where you live, 2.00% to 2.75%, on the first $1,600 of the price only, plus a 2.75% state single article tax on the next $1,600. Many counties also charge a wheel tax with registration.
notes: A private sale is taxed like a dealer sale: 7% state tax on the full price, the local rate on the first $1,600, and the 2.75% state single article tax on the part from $1,600.01 to $3,200 (up to $44).
The title costs $14 (the $5.50 state title fee and the $8.50 county clerk fee). Noting a lien is $11.
The standard plate is $26.50 a year ($19.50 for a motorcycle). All-electric vehicles add $200 for registrations before January 1, 2027 and $274 in 2027. Hybrids and plug-in hybrids add $100.
Trade-in credit applies only when a dealer takes the trade-in and credits it on the invoice.
disclaimers: Estimates only, not tax or legal advice. Verify with your county clerk or the Tennessee Department of Revenue.
If the price is under 75% of the vehicle’s value in a pricing guide, the buyer and seller complete the Affidavit of Non-Dealer Transfers. Without it, or an appraisal, tax is due on the full value.
County wheel taxes and other county clerk fees are not included.
The all-electric vehicle fee rises to $274 for registrations from January 1, 2027.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax on a private car purchase in Tennessee?
faqs.answer: The 7% state rate on the full price, the local rate (2.00% to 2.75%) on the first $1,600, and a 2.75% state single article tax on the part from $1,600.01 to $3,200. On a $15,000 car that is $1,050 state tax, $32 to $44 local tax, and $44 single article tax.

faqs.question: Are private car sales taxed in Tennessee?
faqs.answer: Yes. Occasional sales of most goods are exempt, but a sale of a motor vehicle between individuals is taxable. The county clerk collects the tax when you title the vehicle.

faqs.question: Can I deduct a trade-in on a private vehicle purchase in Tennessee?
faqs.answer: No. Trade-in credit applies only when a dealer takes the trade-in and shows the credit on the invoice. A private sale is taxed on the full price.

faqs.question: How much does a title and plate cost in Tennessee?
faqs.answer: The title is $14 and a lien is $11 more. The standard plate is $26.50 a year, or $19.50 for a motorcycle. All-electric vehicles add $200 ($274 from January 1, 2027), and hybrids and plug-in hybrids add $100. County wheel taxes vary.

faqs.question: I am moving to Tennessee. Do I pay sales tax on my car?
faqs.answer: No, not on a personal vehicle you bring with a genuine move to Tennessee. Register it with your county clerk within 30 days of moving.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Tennessee?
faqs.answer: No. Transfers between spouses, siblings, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, great grandparents and great grandchildren, and the spouses of those lineal relatives are exempt, and so is a gift with nothing given in return. faqs.answer: The title fee is $68.50, plus an $8 handling fee and a local fee of up to $6. Recording a lien costs $10, or $15 with a UCC-1 financing statement.

faqs.question: Do I pay Louisiana vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tax is assessed on the sale price when you title the vehicle in Louisiana. If you buy from an out-of-state seller, show proof the seller lives out of state (such as a copy of their license or a document notarized out of state), or OMV may process it as more than one transfer.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Louisiana?
faqs.answer: No sales or use tax is due on an act of donation, which is signed before a notary and two witnesses (Form DPSMV1699). Transfers by affidavit of heirship, divorce decree, or judgment of possession are also not taxed. Title, handling, and plate fees still apply.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Louisiana?
faqs.answer: Sales tax is due by the 40th day after the sale. After that, a penalty of 5% of the tax for each 30 days applies (up to 25%), plus interest.

kentucky.localTaxNote: Kentucky assesses a flat 6.0% Motor Vehicle Usage Tax statewide (KRS 138.460). No local sales taxes apply to motor vehicles.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle tax rate in Kentucky?
faqs.answer: Kentucky imposes a 6.0% Motor Vehicle Usage Tax (MVUT) under KRS 138.460. Unlike general retail sales, motor vehicles in Kentucky are not subject to local city or county sales taxes.

faqs.question: Does Kentucky allow trade-in credit on private vehicle sales?
faqs.answer: Yes! Under KRS 138.450 and 138.460, trade-in allowances reduce taxable value for private transactions as long as both buyer and seller execute a notarized Affidavit of Total Consideration Given (Form TC 96-182).

faqs.question: How much are Kentucky title and lien fees?
faqs.answer: The Kentucky state certificate of title fee is $9.00. If the purchase is financed through a lender, an additional $22.00 lien filing fee is required by the County Clerk.

faqs.question: How much does vehicle registration cost in Kentucky?
faqs.answer: Standard annual passenger car registration in Kentucky is $21.00. All-electric vehicles pay an additional $120.00 annual electric vehicle fee ($60.00 for hybrids).

faqs.question: Do I pay Kentucky vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: When bringing an out-of-state private vehicle into Kentucky, the state generally assesses its applicable vehicle sales or use tax (6.00%) upon titling and registration. Contact the Kentucky DMV or Department of Revenue to verify eligibility and required documentation before titling.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Kentucky?
faqs.answer: Titling and registration deadlines for private vehicle purchases vary by jurisdiction, typically ranging between 10 to 30 days from the date of purchase. Delaying beyond Kentucky's statutory filing deadline can incur late titling penalty fees and restricts legal operation on public roadways. Check with the Kentucky motor vehicle agency or your local county title office for the exact filing window and penalty schedule.

oregon.label: Oregon

notes: Oregon has no general sales tax and charges 0.0% tax on private party vehicle sales.
Base certificate of title fee is $101.00 under ORS 803.090 for standard passenger vehicles.
Standard passenger vehicle registration is issued on a 2-year biennial term ($126.00 base for 0–19 MPG = $63.00/yr).

disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Oregon Driver and Motor Vehicle Services (DMV).
Oregon does not assess state or local sales tax on private vehicle transactions (0.0% tax).
Title and registration fees vary based on vehicle fuel efficiency rating (MPG) and county of residence.

faqs.question: What is the car sales tax rate in Oregon for private sales?
faqs.answer: Oregon does not have a general sales tax, and private-party vehicle sales between individuals are 100% tax-free (0.0% sales tax). The 0.5% Vehicle Privilege Tax only applies to licensed dealers selling new vehicles.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Oregon?
faqs.answer: Under ORS 803.090, the base Oregon DMV certificate of title fee for standard passenger cars is $101.00. Lien notation is processed on the title application without an extra filing fee.

faqs.question: How are registration fees calculated in Oregon?
faqs.answer: Oregon registers passenger vehicles on a two-year cycle with fees tiered by EPA fuel economy rating, starting at $126.00 for vehicles under 20 MPG ($63.00/year equivalent). Tri-county areas (Multnomah, Washington, Clackamas) add local county fees.

faqs.question: Do electric vehicles pay extra fees in Oregon?
faqs.answer: Yes. All-electric vehicles pay an increased biennial registration fee ($316.00 for 2 years) to compensate for untaxed motor fuel, or owners may enroll in Oregon's voluntary road usage charge program (OReGO).

faqs.question: Do I pay Oregon vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Because Oregon does not levy a statewide vehicle sales or excise tax on private-party transactions, you will not owe state sales tax when titling an out-of-state private purchase in Oregon. Standard certificate of title fees and registration tag fees still apply upon titling.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Oregon?
faqs.answer: In Oregon, private vehicle transfers are not subject to a statewide vehicle sales tax. When transferring title between family members, you only pay standard title transfer fees and registration charges.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Oregon?

Check with the Oregon motor vehicle agency or your local county title office for the exact filing window and penalty schedule.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle tax rate in Oklahoma for private sales?
faqs.answer: A used vehicle pays an excise tax of $20 on the first $1,500 of value and 3.25% of the rest, plus a 1.25% sales tax on the price. On a $15,000 car that is $458.75 excise tax plus $187.50 sales tax.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: Service Oklahoma figures the excise tax on the purchase price or taxable value. A private sale has no trade-in credit to apply.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: A title transfer costs $29.50: the $11 title fee, $17 transfer fee, and $1.50 insurance fee. Recording a lien costs $10. A vehicle titled in another state also needs a $4 VIN inspection.

faqs.question: How are vehicle registration fees calculated in Oklahoma?

faqs.question: Do I pay Oklahoma vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?
faqs.answer: Yes. Take the assigned out-of-state title, Form 701-6, your driver license, proof of Oklahoma insurance, the purchase agreement or Form 722-1, and the vehicle to Service Oklahoma or a licensed operator. You pay the same excise and sales taxes, and the vehicle needs a VIN inspection.

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: A gift between spouses, or between a parent or stepparent and a child or stepchild, is exempt from excise tax with Form 794 (Family Affidavit). It must be a gift, not a sale, and siblings and grandparents do not qualify. Transfers under a divorce decree are also exempt.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: Service Oklahoma requires the title to be applied for within 2 months of obtaining ownership.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Connecticut for private sales?

faqs.question: How is the tax base determined for private sales in Connecticut?

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Connecticut?

faqs.question: How much are Connecticut vehicle title and registration fees?

faqs.question: Do I pay Connecticut vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Connecticut?

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Connecticut?

faqs.question: How much does a vehicle title cost in Utah?

faqs.question: What is the Utah age-based vehicle fee?

faqs.question: Do I pay Utah vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Utah?
faqs.answer: Utah has no sales tax exemption for family-to-family vehicle purchases. Tax is due on sales between family members, on the price actually paid.

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Utah?
faqs.answer: The DMV gives no fixed deadline for a private sale, but you need the title transfer and registration before driving. New residents have 60 days to transfer their titles and registrations.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private vehicle purchase in Iowa?

faqs.question: How much does a vehicle title cost in Iowa?

faqs.question: What fees do I pay when buying a car privately in Nevada?

faqs.question: Do I pay Arkansas vehicle tax if I buy a car from an out-of-state private seller?

faqs.question: Is a vehicle transfer between family members taxable in Arkansas?

faqs.question: How long do I have to title and register a private vehicle purchase in Arkansas?
